answer: Disjoint neighbor path test: before an action is accepted, the agent must return a quartz nonce over k edge-disjoint paths ending in separate neighborhoods; no relay or adjacent peer may repeat across its recent proofs. Enforcement rejects identities whose paths overlap or whose neighbors already served many identities. An attacker pays per identity by provisioning distinct live peers and relays in separate regions, with bandwidth and maintenance costs, and cannot reuse an ivory relay pool. Each new identity needs its own orchard of non-overlapping relays, making bulk creation expensive.
